facts.claim: A marriage licence for a foreign national legally residing in Greece is issued by the competent department of the municipality of residence; the competent body for the procedure is the Ministry of Interior.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr, General Secretariat of Public Administration)
facts.use_note: This registry entry is titled for foreign RESIDENTS of Greece. Do not present it as the route for couples living in Australia.

facts.claim: Waiting period, exact wording: 'the mayor or the president of the community shall wait for one week from the date of submission of the relevant application for any possible objection by third parties'. Deadline of completion: 7 days. The licence is granted 'immediately after expiry of the one-week period' if no objection is lodged.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Official wording is one week, not eight days. Applies to the resident licence.

facts.claim: What starts the clock: the date of submission of the application. Staff check that all supporting documents are present and that the required publication (newspaper notice) has taken place; only then is a protocol number issued. If documents are missing or conditions are not met, the application and documents are returned with instructions and the procedure is repeated.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Procedure steps 2 to 4. Safe phrasing: the week runs from a complete, accepted application; an incomplete file is returned and you start again.

facts.claim: If a third party lodges a written objection (with serious evidence or as a solemn declaration), the mayor immediately invites the applicant to contest it; the licence is granted after hearing the applicant. If the authority refuses the licence, the competent Magistrates' Court decides irrevocably within 10 days of application.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Fee for issuing the marriage licence: EUR 18, e-paravolo (e-Administrative Fee) code 2386, payable by bank cashier, debit or credit card, web banking or Hellenic Post. Approx. AUD: see F-030 for rate.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: A Greek-language search snippet for the separate mitos 'civil marriage licence' entry (Greek citizens, digital gov.gr route) says free of charge; not read in full. Keep EUR 18 tied to the foreign-resident entry.

facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Documents for the foreign-resident licence: certificate of no impediment from the competent consular or other authority; birth certificate translated into Greek; proof of residence in Greece (utility bill or tax notice); passport, residence permit or residence certificate proving lawful residence; divorce decree translated into Greek if applicable; the newspaper issue with the marriage announcement in a local daily of the municipality of residence; passport or birth certificate of the future spouse.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Residents only. Submission in person or by post per the entry; procedure step 1 says in person.

facts.claim: Foreign documents from Hague Convention countries are accepted only with an Apostille and translated into Greek 'by a Greek translator'.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Australia is a Hague Apostille party (DFAT issues apostilles). 'Greek translator' is not further defined here; see translation conflict in needs.

facts.claim: Legal basis: Civil Code articles 1368 to 1370 (PD 456/1984); Law 1250/1982 (introduction of civil marriage); PD 391/1982 (civil marriage ceremonies, licences and certification of civil or religious marriages); Law 5089/2024 (marriage between persons of the same sex).
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Athens Civil Marriages Department serves permanent residents of the City of Athens (Greek citizens, foreigners and refugees) and Greek citizens abroad registered in Athens. The applicant must appear in person with ID to submit documents; a third party with authorisation may collect the licence.
facts.use_note: Athens lists no route for foreigners living abroad on this page.

facts.claim: Athens: 'The marriage license is issued seven (7) days after the submission and verification of the required documents and is valid for six (6) months.'
facts.use_note: Clock starts at submission AND verification. Corroborates F-002.

facts.claim: Athens: all submitted documents must be recent, issued within the last six months; a marital status certificate from the home country (alternative to a divorce certificate) must be issued within the last three months.

Athens, foreign residents: a marriage licence from the home country (if issued), with Apostille, OR a Certificate of No Impediment from the home country or its Embassy in Greece, officially authenticated and translated into Greek; birth certificate officially authenticated and translated into Greek.

Athens newspaper notice: an announcement in a daily Athenian newspaper (one copy for each prospective spouse) stating full names of the couple, parents' full names, place of birth, last place of residence and the municipality of the wedding; if one spouse is a foreign national the information must also be printed in Latin characters.
facts.use_note: No official source found stating the notice must run 'eight days before applying'.

facts.claim: Australian Embassy Athens: a CNI is required by both religious and municipal organisations for each non-Greek citizen marrying in Greece; the acceptable place of issue (Embassy in Greece, DFAT office in Australia, or another Australian mission) can differ significantly between organisations; the application may be lodged with the Embassy in Athens or any DFAT office in Australia for issue in Greece; the CNI is issued in English.
facts.source_date: not shown (page links to an old smartraveller URL, suggesting it has not been updated recently)
